intro: You are standing in Priene, an ancient city in Aydın province from the 4th century BC. This compact Ionian city sits on Mount Mycale, and its grid plan survives intact.
history: Priene was refounded in the Hellenistic period. Because it escaped major Roman rebuilding, what you see here is the purest surviving example of classical town planning.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Temple of Athena and the Bouleuterion, then the Theatre and the Ekklesiasterion.
facts: Did you know? The marble armchairs in the theatre's front row were reserved for city dignitaries. Priene is the best-preserved grid-plan city of antiquity, laid out in squares on a steep slope as if the ground were flat. Pytheos, architect of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, built the Temple of Athena, and Alexander the Great paid for it; the dedication inscription is now in the British Museum. And the council house seated 640, very nearly the city's entire adult male citizenry at once.
outro: This brings our tour of Priene to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Enjoy your visit.
